note: Both sets cover the same core crane-attachment facts (3" std pipe, (2) 3/4" bolts, L3x3x1/4 angle, 1"/1/2"/3/8" plates, 4 X 3/8" cap plate, and the 1'-8" and 1'-4 1/4" heights) and both repeat those facts heavily. Set A additionally captures the PL 4 1/2X4 1/2X1/2 plate that B omits, but it pads its sample with label-contaminated values ('3/8 PL TYP', '1 PL TYP', '1/2 PL TYP', '3 DIA STD. PIPE', '3 DIA', '3/4 DIA') and states each fact up to four times. Set B is cleaner and more compact, though it invents a 'thickness/gap' attribute for the unlabeled 1/4" dimension. On balance B carries fewer wrong claims despite missing one real plate size.
remarks: Both sets miss the 11'-4" T.O. STEEL elevation shown in the detail, and neither binds the standalone 3/8" and 1/4" dimension callouts on the left to a specific feature. Set A's misreads are mostly label-in-value formatting ('3/8 PL TYP' as a thickness), i.e. low-severity but counted per the misread category; its worst structural problem is duplication (plate 3/8" x4, pipe 3" x4, angle L3x3x1/4 x4, bolts 3/4" x4). Set B's 1/4" claim is unsupported as stated: the page shows 1/4" only as an unlabeled dimension, with no 'thickness/gap' attribute. Both use the vague entity 'structural element' for the two vertical dimensions, which are really heights/elevations of the attachment assembly.
